title: Vector Embeddings & Semantic Spaces
source_excerpt:
1. Vector Embeddings & Semantic Spaces

What you will learn: Vector embeddings transform text into dense numerical coordinate arrays where semantic meaning correlates with geometric distance. Unlike keyword matching, embeddings capture conceptual relationships, synonyms, and context in multi-thousand-dimensional vector manifolds.

title: Cosine Similarity vs Dot Product vs Euclidean
source_excerpt:
2. Cosine Similarity vs Dot Product vs Euclidean

What you will learn: Vector proximity metrics evaluate semantic relatedness: Cosine similarity measures the angle between vectors (length-invariant), Dot product measures angle and magnitude (optimal for normalized embeddings), and Euclidean distance measures straight-line coordinate distance.

title: The Naive RAG Pipeline
source_excerpt:
3. The Naive RAG Pipeline

What you will learn: The standard Naive RAG architecture consists of three steps: Ingestion (chunking and indexing documents into a vector database), Retrieval (finding top-k similar chunks for a user query), and Generation (passing retrieved chunks to an LLM as prompt context).

title: Limitations of Naive RAG & Hallucination Points
source_excerpt:
4. Limitations of Naive RAG & Hallucination Points

What you will learn: Naive RAG suffers from retrieval failure modes: retrieving irrelevant chunks due to semantic mismatch, missing key context split across boundaries, returning redundant duplicates, and LLMs hallucinating when retrieved passages contain contradictory facts.

title: Choosing Embedding Models (MTEB Leaderboard)
source_excerpt:
5. Choosing Embedding Models (MTEB Leaderboard)

What you will learn: Selecting an embedding model requires evaluating performance on the Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (MTEB) across retrieval, clustering, and reranking tasks, while balancing embedding dimension size, context window length, and inference latency.

title: Fixed-Size vs Recursive Character Chunking
source_excerpt:
6. Fixed-Size vs Recursive Character Chunking

What you will learn: Fixed-size chunking splits text at arbitrary character counts, often severing sentences mid-thought. Recursive character splitting splits hierarchically by paragraphs, double newlines, single newlines, and spaces, preserving natural grammatical boundaries.

title: Semantic & Document-Aware Chunking
source_excerpt:
7. Semantic & Document-Aware Chunking

What you will learn: Semantic chunking monitors embedding distance between adjacent sentences and creates chunk breaks when semantic similarity drops sharply. Document-aware chunking parses markdown headers, HTML DOM structures, or code blocks to preserve structural context.

title: Chunk Overlap & Boundary Preservation
source_excerpt:
8. Chunk Overlap & Boundary Preservation

What you will learn: Applying a 10-20% sliding window overlap between consecutive chunks ensures that concepts spanning chunk boundaries are captured in at least one retrieved passage, preventing loss of relational context.

title: Multi-Modal Document Parsing (PDFs, Tables, OCR)
source_excerpt:
9. Multi-Modal Document Parsing (PDFs, Tables, OCR)

What you will learn: Real-world documents contain multi-column layouts, tables, and images. Using specialized parsers that extract clean markdown tables, preserve reading order, and OCR embedded figures prevents table data from being garbled into unsearchable text strings.

title: Extracting & Storing Rich Metadata
source_excerpt:
10. Extracting & Storing Rich Metadata

What you will learn: Enriching chunks with metadata (source document ID, creation date, author, department, section title, page number) enables structured metadata filtering during vector retrieval, ensuring queries only search relevant document subsets.

title: Flat Index vs Approximate Nearest Neighbors (ANN)
source_excerpt:
11. Flat Index vs Approximate Nearest Neighbors (ANN)

What you will learn: A Flat index computes exact distance against every vector in the database (O(N) search time). For millions of vectors, Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) indexing trades negligible precision for logarithmic O(log N) search speed and millisecond response times.

title: Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW)
source_excerpt:
12. Hierarchical Navigable Small World (HNSW)

What you will learn: HNSW organizes vectors into a multi-layer graph where top layers have sparse long-distance links for fast routing and bottom layers have dense local links for fine-grained nearest neighbor search, providing state-of-the-art ANN recall and speed.

title: Inverted File with Product Quantization (IVF-PQ)
source_excerpt:
13. Inverted File with Product Quantization (IVF-PQ)

What you will learn: IVF partitions vector space into Voronoi clusters to restrict search to nearby centroids, while Product Quantization compresses vectors into short byte codes, reducing RAM consumption by up to 90% in large-scale deployments.

title: Vector Database Architectures (Pinecone, Qdrant, Milvus, Chroma)
source_excerpt:
14. Vector Database Architectures (Pinecone, Qdrant, Milvus, Chroma)

What you will learn: Dedicated vector databases offer distinct architectures: Pinecone provides managed serverless scaling, Qdrant is written in Rust for high-throughput payload filtering, Milvus excels in massive distributed clusters, and Chroma offers simple embedded local storage.

title: Index Maintenance, CRUD & Sharding
source_excerpt:
15. Index Maintenance, CRUD & Sharding

What you will learn: Production vector databases require live document updates and deletions. Managing incremental indexing, soft deletes, and horizontal database sharding across nodes ensures high availability and low search latency under write-heavy loads.

title: Hybrid Search: Sparse (BM25) + Dense (Vector)
source_excerpt:
16. Hybrid Search: Sparse (BM25) + Dense (Vector)

What you will learn: Dense vector search excels at conceptual matching but struggles with exact acronyms, product SKUs, and unique IDs. Hybrid search combines sparse lexical BM25 retrieval with dense vector search using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) for optimal recall.

title: Parent Document & Auto-Merging Retrievers
source_excerpt:
17. Parent Document & Auto-Merging Retrievers

What you will learn: Parent document retrieval indexes small granular child chunks (e.g. 100 tokens) for vector matching accuracy, but retrieves the larger parent section (e.g. 1000 tokens) to provide the LLM with complete contextual narrative.

title: Sentence Window Retrieval
source_excerpt:
18. Sentence Window Retrieval

What you will learn: Sentence window retrieval embeds individual single sentences for pinpoint vector search accuracy, but returns a sliding context window of surrounding sentences (e.g. 3 sentences before and after) to the generation prompt.

title: Multi-Query Generation & Query Expansion
source_excerpt:
19. Multi-Query Generation & Query Expansion

What you will learn: User queries are often brief or ambiguous. Using an LLM to generate 3-5 alternative phrasings and perspectives of the user query expands retrieval coverage and retrieves relevant documents that used different vocabulary.

title: Contextual Compression & Filtering
source_excerpt:
20. Contextual Compression & Filtering

What you will learn: Instead of passing raw retrieved chunks directly to the generator, contextual compression uses a small model to extract only the sentences strictly relevant to the query, stripping out irrelevant noise and saving prompt tokens.

title: Query Rewriting & Disambiguation
source_excerpt:
21. Query Rewriting & Disambiguation

What you will learn: Conversational queries often rely on pronouns or prior turns (e.g., 'What about its price?'). Query rewriting inspects conversation history and rewrites the query into a standalone, fully disambiguated search statement.

title: Step-Back Prompting for Broader Context
source_excerpt:
22. Step-Back Prompting for Broader Context

What you will learn: Step-back prompting generates a higher-level, more abstract query (e.g., from 'Why did my Physics exam question 3 fail?' to 'What are the core laws of thermodynamics?'), retrieving foundational principles alongside specific facts.

title: Sub-Query Decomposition for Multi-Hop QA
source_excerpt:
23. Sub-Query Decomposition for Multi-Hop QA

What you will learn: Complex questions (e.g., 'Compare the battery life of iPhone 15 and Pixel 8') require multiple retrieval steps. Decomposing the prompt into independent sub-queries searches for each entity separately before synthesizing.

title: Semantic Routing across Multiple Indexes
source_excerpt:
24. Semantic Routing across Multiple Indexes

What you will learn: Enterprise systems maintain diverse data stores (SQL databases, product manuals, legal contracts). Semantic routers classify query intent and route requests to the most appropriate specialized index or retriever.

title: Fallback Strategies & Web Search Augmentation
source_excerpt:
25. Fallback Strategies & Web Search Augmentation

What you will learn: When vector similarity scores fall below a minimum relevance threshold, the system triggers fallback routines—such as querying a live search engine API or prompting the user for clarification—preventing ungrounded hallucinations.

title: Query Intent Classification
source_excerpt:
26. Query Intent Classification

What you will learn: Classifying whether a user query requires real-time facts, static knowledge, code execution, or general chit-chat allows bypassing unnecessary vector retrieval entirely for conversational messages, reducing overall system latency.

title: Cross-Encoder vs Bi-Encoder Architecture
source_excerpt:
27. Cross-Encoder vs Bi-Encoder Architecture

What you will learn: Bi-encoders encode queries and documents separately into vectors for fast search. Cross-encoders process the query and document together through full cross-attention layers, computing precise deep semantic relevance scores.

title: Cohere & BGE Reranker Models
source_excerpt:
28. Cohere & BGE Reranker Models

What you will learn: Deploying a neural reranker model (like Cohere Rerank or BGE-Reranker) as a second-stage filter over the top-50 initial retrieved candidates dramatically improves top-k precision and filters out superficial vector false positives.

title: Lost in the Middle: Mitigating Primacy/Recency Bias
source_excerpt:
29. Lost in the Middle: Mitigating Primacy/Recency Bias

What you will learn: Language models pay highest attention to tokens at the very beginning and very end of their prompt context window. Information placed in the middle of long contexts is frequently ignored (the 'lost in the middle' effect).

title: Context Pruning & Dynamic Truncation
source_excerpt:
30. Context Pruning & Dynamic Truncation

What you will learn: Context pruning removes redundant sentences and filler phrases from retrieved passages while preserving core factual assertions, maximizing the density of useful information within the LLM's prompt window.

title: Citation Generation & Grounded Attributions
source_excerpt:
31. Citation Generation & Grounded Attributions

What you will learn: Instructing the LLM to include inline citation markers (e.g., [Doc-1, Page 4]) grounded strictly in retrieved context enables users to verify factual claims and audit model assertions against primary sources.

title: Re-ordering Chunks for LLM Attention
source_excerpt:
32. Re-ordering Chunks for LLM Attention

What you will learn: To counteract primacy and recency biases, strategic chunk re-ordering algorithms place the most critically relevant passages at the top and bottom of the context prompt, leaving background context in the center.

title: Self-RAG: Reflection Tokens & Self-Assessment
source_excerpt:
33. Self-RAG: Reflection Tokens & Self-Assessment

What you will learn: Self-RAG trains models to generate special reflection tokens to critique their own output: assessing whether retrieval is needed, evaluating whether retrieved passages are relevant, and verifying if generated claims are supported.

title: Corrective RAG (CRAG) & Document Grading
source_excerpt:
34. Corrective RAG (CRAG) & Document Grading

What you will learn: CRAG introduces an automated evaluator that scores retrieved documents. If confidence is high, it refines the text; if confidence is low, it discards the chunks and triggers an external web search to correct the knowledge gap.

title: Adaptive RAG: Deciding When to Retrieve
source_excerpt:
35. Adaptive RAG: Deciding When to Retrieve

What you will learn: Not every query needs retrieval. Adaptive RAG uses query complexity classifiers to dynamically route simple queries to direct generation, moderate queries to single-step RAG, and complex multi-hop queries to iterative agentic search.

title: GraphRAG: Knowledge Graphs for Global Sensemaking
source_excerpt:
36. GraphRAG: Knowledge Graphs for Global Sensemaking

What you will learn: Vector RAG struggles with holistic questions (e.g., 'What are the primary themes in this 500-page dataset?'). GraphRAG extracts entities, relationships, and community summaries into a Knowledge Graph for comprehensive thematic retrieval.

title: Multi-Agent RAG with Specialized Researcher Agents
source_excerpt:
37. Multi-Agent RAG with Specialized Researcher Agents

What you will learn: Multi-agent RAG coordinates specialized sub-agents: a query planner, multiple parallel searchers querying diverse databases, a fact-checker verifying citations, and a synthesizer composing the final response.

title: Tool-Augmented Retrieval with SQL & APIs
source_excerpt:
38. Tool-Augmented Retrieval with SQL & APIs

What you will learn: Combining vector retrieval with relational SQL query generation (Text-to-SQL) allows systems to answer questions requiring both unstructured narrative context and precise numerical calculations.

title: The RAG Triad: Context Relevance, Groundedness, Answer Relevance
source_excerpt:
39. The RAG Triad: Context Relevance, Groundedness, Answer Relevance

What you will learn: Evaluating RAG systems requires measuring three core pillars: Context Relevance (did retrieval fetch relevant chunks?), Groundedness (is the answer derived strictly from context?), and Answer Relevance (did the answer address user intent?).

title: RAGAS & TruLens Automated Evaluation
source_excerpt:
40. RAGAS & TruLens Automated Evaluation

What you will learn: Frameworks like RAGAS and TruLens compute mathematical scores for fidelity, answer correctness, and semantic similarity using automated LLM-assisted evaluation pipelines without requiring manual human labeling.

title: Synthetic Test Set Generation
source_excerpt:
41. Synthetic Test Set Generation

What you will learn: Generating diverse synthetic question-context-answer test sets from domain documents creates comprehensive evaluation suites that test edge cases, multi-hop reasoning, and out-of-domain rejection capabilities.

title: Caching Strategies (Semantic Cache, Exact Cache)
source_excerpt:
42. Caching Strategies (Semantic Cache, Exact Cache)

What you will learn: Exact caching matches identical query strings, while semantic caching uses vector similarity to return cached answers for semantically equivalent queries (e.g. 'How to reset password' vs 'Password reset steps'), slashing API costs.

title: Latency Budgeting & Streaming RAG Pipelines
source_excerpt:
43. Latency Budgeting & Streaming RAG Pipelines

What you will learn: Streaming generation tokens immediately to the user while performing background retrieval and asynchronous reranking creates responsive user experiences and reduces perceived latency in production applications.

title: Security & Access-Control-Aware Retrieval
source_excerpt:
44. Security & Access-Control-Aware Retrieval

What you will learn: Enterprise RAG must enforce Document-Level Security (DLS). Pre-filtering vector search results by user security roles and permission groups guarantees users never retrieve unauthorized documents.
